changeability.rationale: The domain logic with real bug risk (sprites, alternate-form filtering, dedupe, stat/move mapping) is commendably centralized, so those fixes land in one place. But UI conventions (page titles, type badges, dex numbers, not-found handling) are copy-pasted across route files, so a format change means four to six edits.

app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:16 — `loader({ params, request }: any)` and `{ loaderData }: any` (also move.tsx:5, ability.tsx:5, type-detail.tsx:5) discard the loader→component contract instead of using generated Route types

coupling.rationale: Structural coupling is low: a clean server/client seam, narrow component props, shared state only via the URL. The `any`-typed loaders and components in four of seven routes are the main tangle — refactors of loader return shapes won't be caught by the compiler.

evidence: app/app/lib/api.server.ts:150 — cardsFromRefs encapsulates alternate-form exclusion, dedupe and dex sort once for three pages
app/app/components.tsx:43 — PokemonGrid stretches across home, move, ability, type pages, but via a boolean showTypes flag
app/app/routes/move.tsx:5-22 — loader+meta+notFound boilerplate repeated per resource; no resource-page abstraction to instantiate for an Items section
app/app/lib/api.server.ts:421-487 — getMovePage/getAbilityPage/getTypePage are bespoke builders in one 490-line module; adding a resource means appending another
app/app/routes/pokemon.tsx:178 — MovesTable hard-codes its column set rather than parameterizing over row shape
abstraction_design.rationale: The card/list abstraction is genuinely designed around the app's real variation, but resource pages are a copy-paste pattern rather than a seam: an Items section reuses helpers yet still duplicates the route-module boilerplate, and the data layer funnels everything through a single growing file.

findings.issue: Loaders, components and meta in 4 of 7 routes are typed `any` (also move.tsx:5, ability.tsx:5, type-detail.tsx:5) instead of the framework's generated `Route.LoaderArgs` / `Route.ComponentProps` / `Route.MetaArgs` from `./+types/...`; the loader→component contract is untyped, so renaming a data field or changing a shape compiles fine and breaks at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Import the generated route types (`import type { Route } from './+types/pokemon'`) and use `Route.LoaderArgs`, `Route.ComponentProps`, `Route.MetaArgs` in every route module, as home.tsx and types.tsx already do via `Awaited<ReturnType<typeof loader>>`.

findings.issue: The `data ?? { notFound: true as const }` sentinel plus a component-side `if (data.notFound)` branch is duplicated in four route files, diverging from the framework-mode idiom (throw a 404 from the loader, render via ErrorBoundary), never sends an HTTP 404, and must be copied by every future resource page.
findings.suggestion: Throw `data('Not Found', { status: 404 })` in the loader and render the shared NotFoundPage from a single root-level ErrorBoundary; delete the sentinel checks and the `notFound` meta ternaries.

findings.issue: The `<title> – Pokédex` convention is duplicated across six meta functions (pokemon.tsx:17, move.tsx:14, ability.tsx:13, type-detail.tsx:14, types.tsx:9, not-found.tsx:4); changing the title format or wording means six edits.
findings.suggestion: Add a `pageTitle(text?: string)` helper in a shared module returning `[{ title: text ? `${text} – Pokédex` : 'Pokédex' }]` and use it in every meta.

findings.issue: TypeBadge only renders a span, so the link variant is inlined with the `type-badge type-${name}` class scheme in five places (pokemon.tsx:89, pokemon.tsx:273, move.tsx:32, type-detail.tsx:37, types.tsx:20); restyling or adding behavior to type badges touches six sites.
findings.suggestion: Extend TypeBadge (or add a small `TypeBadgeLink`) that renders as a `<Link to={`/types/${name}`} className={...}>` and use it everywhere a type name appears.

findings.issue: Dead exports: `getTypeInfos`, `getGenerationInfos` and `spriteUrlForId` (api.server.ts:114) are exported but never imported by any route; a future editor must check whether they're part of a public surface.
findings.suggestion: Un-export them (they're only used internally) or delete if the abstraction isn't needed.

findings.issue: cardSprite hard-codes the `id <= 1025` shipped-snapshot threshold as data-source knowledge in code, with a fallback fetch for live-overlay additions; if the snapshot changes the threshold is silently wrong.
findings.suggestion: Derive the fast path from something the API states (or always consult the pokemon record, with the pattern as fallback), and isolate the threshold in one named, commented constant.

findings.issue: api.server.ts is a single 490-line module holding the HTTP client, cache, three derived indexes, and bespoke page-data builders for all five page types; extending (e.g. an Items section) or changing caching rules means editing many concerns in one file.
findings.suggestion: Split into a small `api/client.ts` (fetchJson/getRecord/getList/recordCache) plus per-resource modules (species.ts, move.ts, type.ts, ...) that import it; the promise-cache invalidation would then live in one place.

findings.issue: PokemonGrid already carries a `showTypes` boolean flag; adding name-sorting or hidden-ability variants would grow the flag set.
findings.suggestion: Prefer composing small pieces (a CardTypes fragment, an optional sort applied in the data layer) over accumulating boolean props.

findings.issue: Dex-number formatting is inlined (`#${String(data.id).padStart(4, '0')}`) even though the `dexNumber` helper exists at lib/format.ts:11 and is used in components.tsx.

summary: The data layer is the strong point: one server-only module owns all API knowledge, and sprite/card/alternate-form logic is centralized so the hardest bug classes fix in exactly one place. Editability cost is concentrated in the route files, where the not-found sentinel, title convention, type-badge markup and `any`-typed loader/component contracts are copy-pasted four to six times, and in the framework-typed-idiom gap (no generated Route types, no ErrorBoundary 404s). Extending to a new resource section means duplicating boilerplate rather than instantiating an abstraction.
